analysis.title: GS Stankard - Eq Positioning and Key Levels 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS model estimates CTAs are long about $43.5bn of global equities, down from $125bn a month ago and $67bn last week.

Baseline CTA flow forecast is a sale of $3.5bn of global equities over the coming week if prices and vol persist. In the US the model expects $5.5bn of buying from SPX and NDX, where all modeled trend signals remain positive.
CTA flow is roughly symmetric around the baseline: the community buys $23bn in a large up move and sells $26bn in a large down move over one week.

GS prime brokerage data shows global equities net sold (-0.3 SDs 1-year), with short sales outpacing long buys 1.3 to 1. US equities were slightly net sold (-0.1 SDs 1-year), driven by single-stock short sales.
Info Tech was the most net sold US sector (-1.0 SDs 1-year) after being the most net bought US sector in 4 of the past 5 weeks. The selling came from both long and short sales.
US-listed ETF shorts rose 4.4% on the week and 6.2% month/month, led by Large Cap Equity and Tech ETFs, partly offset by covering in Financials ETFs.

Hedge funds net bought US Industrials at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SDs 1-year) after selling for 5 consecutive weeks. The buying was almost entirely long buys, led by Aerospace & Defense, Construction & Engineering, Airlines and Industrial Conglomerates.

Hedge funds cut risk in US Health Care for a 4th straight week, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.6 to 1. Biotech has seen the largest dollar de-grossing of any US subsector since mid-August, and its trailing 8-week de-grossing is the largest in more than five years.
Fundamental L/S net leverage is at the 6th percentile 1-year, US L/S net leverage is at the 2nd percentile, and the US Fundamental long/short ratio is at the 1st percentile on a five-year view.

Corporate buyback activity on the GS desk stayed light in pre-earnings blackout, at 0.8x 2025 YTD ADTV. GS expects volumes and discretionary open-market repurchases to pick up as earnings season starts this week, with about 10% of corporates in an open window by the end of the week.
The median S&P 500 stock trades 16% below its high, pushing market breadth to its lowest level since the Dot-Com Bubble.

sector_views.rationale: Most net sold US sector by hedge funds this week (-1.0 SDs 1-year), after being the most net bought in 4 of the past 5 weeks. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.
Hedge funds net bought at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SDs 1-year) after 5 straight weeks of selling. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.
Hedge funds de-grossed for a 4th straight week, and Biotech de-grossing since mid-August is the largest in more than five years. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.

earnings_insights: Earnings season starts this week, led by major Financials. GS expects corporates to exit buyback blackout about 1-2 days after their releases, with about 10% in an open window by the end of the week.
risk_factors: Market breadth is at its weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble, with the median S&P 500 stock 16% below its high.
CTA length has shrunk sharply, and a large down move would trigger roughly $26bn of selling over one week and $143.84bn over one month, including $65.79bn out of the US.
Hedge fund net leverage is at very low percentiles (US L/S net 2nd percentile 1-year), and short sales are outpacing long buys.
Light buyback activity in blackout removes a source of demand until corporates reopen their windows after earnings.
charts_described: Market breadth chart: the median S&P 500 stock trades 16% below its respective high, the lowest breadth since the Dot-Com Bubble.
vol_and_positioning: CTA long exposure in global equities is estimated at $43.5bn, versus $125bn one month ago and $67bn last week.
One-week CTA flow scenarios: flat tape sells $3.64bn globally (buys $5.27bn into the US), up tape buys $23.24bn (US $6.39bn), down tape sells $26.07bn (US outflow $936mm).
One-month CTA flow scenarios: flat tape buys $5.97bn globally (US $8.39bn), up tape buys $136.81bn (US $24.53bn), down tape sells $143.84bn (US outflow $65.79bn).
SPX CTA pivot levels are 7704 short term, 7493 medium term and 7012 long term.

Overall hedge fund book gross leverage rose 0.7 pts to 308.7% (60th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 1.5 pts to 75.9% (10th percentile 1-year). L/S ratio fell 1.2% to 1.652 (14th percentile 1-year).

Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 3.3 pts to 209.5% (43rd percentile) and net leverage fell 0.2 pts to 52.9% (6th percentile). US L/S gross leverage rose 3.8 pts to 213% (53rd percentile) and US L/S net leverage rose 0.5 pts to 46.9% (2nd percentile), its first increase in four weeks.
US Fundamental long/short ratio (market value) fell 0.3% to 1.565, the 1st percentile on a five-year view.

GS Equity Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell 0.70% from 10/2 to 10/8 versus MSCI World TR +0.78%, driven by alpha losses on both long and short sides. The Systematic L/S estimate rose 0.82%, with alpha of +0.55% from short side gains and beta of +0.27%.

Charts in focus include Market Breadth, US Panic Index, Risk Appetite Indicator, SPX vs. Singles Skew, Call Skew vs. Put Skew, S&P Futures Liquidity, Funding Spreads vs S&P 500 and S&P 500 Implied Correlation.

tension_points.bull_case: All modeled CTA trend signals in SPX and NDX remain positive, and GS expects $5.5bn of US buying from those two indices even as the global baseline is a $3.5bn sale.
tension_points.bear_case: CTA length is down to $43.5bn from $125bn a month ago, and a large down move would trigger about $26bn of selling over one week and $143.84bn over one month.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SPX falling through the CTA pivot levels of 7704 (short term), 7493 (medium term) and 7012 (long term).
